key_insight: A composite World Model combines spiking neural memory with transformers to track material history and predict responses of locally variable, defective composites within a nonlinear finite-element solver.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets lower-cost structural simulations that retain local material architecture and irreversible state without repeatedly solving expensive material-scale models.
method: Encode local material architecture, including defects.
Combine SNN memory for long-term material state with transformer blocks for short-term strain history.
Train in three stages, including recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling, then disassemble the model for FE-solver integration.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks against IM7/8552 laminate experiments under tension, compression and transverse shear, covering pristine and wrinkled composites, report prediction errors of 0.4%–4.8%.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify solver speedup or per-integration-point memory use, leaving large-scale computational savings to be verified.
paper_title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
